head.title: Desert Dinner Party Dubai: Planning Guide | myCHEF
head.h1: Desert Dinner Party Dubai: Planning Guide
head.meta_description: Plan a desert dinner party in Dubai with practical guidance on venue permission, access, cooking facilities, menus and service.

opening_paragraph: A desert dinner party in Dubai begins with a suitable, authorised location and a clear plan for reaching it. Once the site is agreed, the chef can develop a menu and service that suit the facilities, weather and time of day.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Confirm the site before the menu
replace_in_block.new_heading: Confirm the site before the menu
new_paragraphs: Ask the site owner or operator to confirm permission for your event, external catering, vehicles and any proposed cooking equipment. Obtain the relevant requirements directly rather than assuming an open area is available for private use.
Confirm the arrival route, parking, unloading distance, toilets, lighting, water and power. If the site changes, the catering plan may need to change too.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Choose food suited to the setting
replace_in_block.new_heading: Choose food suited to the setting
new_paragraphs: Arabic sharing dishes, grilled food and slow-cooked mains can suit a desert table, but the cooking method depends on the facilities and permissions. A permitted live grill needs a suitable work area and an agreed safety plan; a prepared menu may be more practical elsewhere.

Agree the setup time, guest arrival, meal service and finish before the event. The proposal should state how wind, heat or an unsuitable forecast will be handled, including any alternative location or postponement terms.

myCHEF BBQ and live-station formats start from AED 150 per person, while bespoke chef-led plated dining is AED 700–950. Site hire, transport, equipment and other outdoor requirements can materially affect the total and must be confirmed separately.

Compare the complete service, including the menu, guest count, preparation, staffing, equipment, delivery and clear-down. A per-person price is useful only when the inclusions are clear. Ask which elements are fixed and which can change if your plans change.

Share allergies and other dietary requirements before confirming. The culinary partner should explain the preparation arrangements and any remaining cross-contact risk. Review the payment schedule, cancellation terms and change deadlines in your written booking.

Send the date, Dubai address, expected guest count and preferred service time, together with your menu ideas and venue details. Photos of the kitchen or service area can help the team assess what is practical.

myCHEF typically replies within 15 minutes between 9am and 11pm Dubai time. The tailored proposal follows once the requirements and availability have been reviewed. A first reply is an acknowledgement, rather than confirmation that a chef or date has been secured.
